newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's net foreign debt rises to $21.6 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's net foreign debt rises to $21.6 bln.

text.p: South Korean net foreign debt -- foreign debt minus overseas assets -- rose to $21.6 billion at the end of March from $17.1 billion at end-1995 and $14.5 billion a year ago, the central Bank of Korea said on Monday.
A bank official said the rise was attributable to the widening current account deficit, which was $11.7 billion for the first seven months of this year against $6.5 billion a year earlier.
The nation's total foreign debt at the end of March stood at $86.2 billion, up from $78.4 billion at the end of 1995 and $63.1 billion a year before.
On the other hand, overseas assets held by South Koreans rose to $64.6 billion at the end of March from $61.4 billion at the end of 1995 and $48.6 billion a year ago.
South Korean net foreign debt rose to a peak of $35.5 billion at the end of 1985 and fell to a low of $3 billion at the end of 1989.
But the bank said net foreign debt began to increase again as a result of the accumulating current account deficit since then.
